_comment: What this site is allowed to SAY about prices and the free trial.
In one week this repo published four different descriptions of the same offer:
a FAQ promising the Essential plan 'free for 1 month', a plan badge promising
'free for 1 month', a call-to-action claiming 'card required at sign-up' four
inches from a signup page reading 'No credit card required', and an assistant
reporting a '60-day free trial'. The truth was 14 days, no card, every plan.
Two had been live for months, on a site taking payment.
None of them appeared in a diff, which is why review after review walked past
them: they were not changes, they were statements that stopped being true while
nobody was looking at them. That is the class of defect this file exists to end.
KEEP THIS HONEST. Every figure below is the amount Stripe actually charges,
confirmed against the LIVE account on 2026-08-09. If a price changes in Stripe
and not here, this file becomes the new lie and the check goes green over it —
which is exactly why `verifyAgainstStripe` exists (see below).

_trialDays_comment: 14 days, from the organisations.trial_ends_at column default (migration 00027).
⚠️ Subscribing currently grants a FURTHER 14-day Stripe trial on top of this, so
a customer can reach ~28 free days in two stages. That is an open product
question on SCRUM-393, not a licence to state a longer number here: 14 is what
a new account gets, and it is what every surface should say until Karen decides.

_roots_comment: The surfaces that make claims to a visitor. Deliberately NOT the whole repo:
the dashboard quotes project costs and estimates, which are outputs of the
product rather than statements about what it costs to buy.
_verifyAgainstStripe_comment: OFF, and this is a real cost that should not be glossed: with it off, the prices
above are unverified, and if one changes in Stripe this file quietly becomes the
new source of the error while the check keeps reporting green. The whole point of
the option is that the authority should be the money, not this JSON.
It is off only because turning it on requires a Stripe key in CI, and a LIVE
secret key in Actions for a read-only price check is the wrong trade. The right
fix is a RESTRICTED key with read access to Prices and nothing else — a few
minutes in the Stripe dashboard — then set this true and add STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
to the repo secrets. Until then the figures above were checked by hand, once,
on the date in the comment at the top, which works exactly once.
